references.text: Continuous strategy: The instruction to call oneself 'your servant' (32:19) is directly carried out and confirmed in the meeting itself (33:5).
Cohesive text: 32:19 is a direct continuation of the instructions given in 32:5.
Cause and effect: The fear of Esau's army (32:7) triggers the diplomatic gift and submission in 32:19.
Thematic contrast: Jacob's use of identity/manipulation against Esau (27:19) stands in sharp contrast to his humble submission toward him later (32:19).
Thematic parallel: Gift-giving as a strategy to win favor ('grace') from a potential enemy (Jacob/Esau vs. Abigail/David).
Continuation of the dialogue: The instruction to call oneself 'your servant' (32:19) is actively used in the negotiation for grace in 33:15.
Theological contrast: Jacob is made 'lord' in 27:37, but voluntarily chooses to be 'servant' to Esau in 32:19 to achieve peace.
Narrative connection: The gift proposed in 32:19 is received and acknowledged as God's blessing in 33:11.
Thematic parallel: Humility ('servant') and gift-giving as means to win favor from a powerful counterpart (Jacob/Esau vs. Abigail/David).
